observations: Photo 0: Close-up of a black lens barrel, front ring text reads 'AF-S NIKKOR' and '50mm 1:8G', mount area shows 'Nikon' branding, aperture ring visible.
Photo 1: Same lens held in a hand, text again reads 'AF-S NIKKOR 50mm 1:8G', 'Nikon' engraving visible, watermark 'OLAJIDE AMOS BISHOP' overlaid.
Photo 2: Lens lying with a lens hood and a second lens cap, same 'AF-S NIKKOR 50mm 1:8G' and 'Nikon' text clearly legible on the barrel.
No box, no receipt, no serial number plate, no caps shown separately with model info, no test/sample image shown.
A second lens body appears in the background of photos 0-2, possibly the item being advertised or a different lens entirely.

claims.claim: American used lens, clean and pure like new
claims.evidence: Origin and usage history cannot be confirmed from photos; cosmetic condition looks clean but 'like new' functional claim cannot be tested remotely.
All three photos clearly show 'AF-S NIKKOR 50mm 1.8G' engraved on the lens barrel, not 60mm.

risks.risk: Seller's stated focal length (60mm) does not match the engraved focal length (50mm) seen in every photo, suggesting a possible bait-and-switch or mismatched listing.
risks.proof: A photo of the exact lens to be shipped, with focal length and serial number clearly legible, matched to a video confirming autofocus and aperture function.
risks.if_unproven: treat as misrepresented item; price only the lens as actually shown (50mm f/1.8G), not as a 60mm lens

risks.risk: Functional condition (autofocus motor, aperture blades, glass clarity/fungus) cannot be verified from static photos.
risks.proof: A short video showing autofocus racking, aperture blades closing/opening, and a clear shot through the glass against light.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working, i.e. worst case functional condition

risks.risk: No serial number or box shown, so authenticity (genuine Nikon vs third-party clone) cannot be confirmed.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the serial number and mount contacts, compared to Nikon's official serial format.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified authenticity, not assumed genuine premium stock

risks.risk: A second lens visible in the background photos is unexplained; unclear if it is included or a different unit altogether, causing confusion about what is actually for sale.
risks.proof: A single clear photo of only the item being sold, with all accessories laid out together.
risks.if_unproven: price only the single lens matching the engraved 50mm 1.8G, exclude the background item

proof_requests: Please re-confirm the exact focal length and show a clear photo of the engraving alongside the seller's claim of '60mm' — the photos show '50mm 1.8G'.
Send a short video of the lens autofocus and aperture blades in action.
Photo of the serial number and front/rear element close-up for fungus/scratch check.
Clarify what is included in the sale (hood, caps, second lens visible in background).
response.reason: The seller's core claim that this is a '60mm' lens is directly contradicted by all three photos, which clearly show 'AF-S NIKKOR 50mm 1.8G' engraved on the lens; this mismatch between the advertised model and the photographed model is a classic sign of a misleading or bait-and-switch listing, so a reliable price cannot be assigned until the discrepancy is resolved.
